title: Maine's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Maine's 2nd Congressional District is an open seat following the retirement of Democratic incumbent Jared Golden. The general election pits former two-term Republican Governor Paul LePage against the winner of a competitive four-way Democratic primary that was unresolved after the June 9 primary and headed to ranked-choice tabulation. This rural, sprawling district covering most of northern and eastern Maine has trended Republican in recent presidential elections — Donald Trump carried it in both 2020 and 2024 — making it a top national target for both parties as they compete for control of the U.S. House. The race will test whether a moderate or progressive Democratic nominee can hold the seat against a well-known Republican former governor.
polling_note: Only primary polling was found; no general-election head-to-head polls between LePage and any Democrat were publicly available at time of research.

candidates.name: Paul LePage
candidates.summary: Paul LePage served two terms as Governor of Maine from 2011 to 2019 and was previously the mayor of Waterville. He ran unopposed for the Republican nomination in Maine's 2nd Congressional District after incumbent Democrat Jared Golden announced his retirement. LePage is a conservative known for his blunt style and efforts to cut taxes and reduce government regulation.

candidates.name: Joe Baldacci
candidates.summary: Joe Baldacci is a three-term Maine State Senator representing District 9 and is the son of former Maine Governor John Baldacci. He served as Mayor of Bangor from 2008 to 2012 and has practiced law for over 30 years. Baldacci is considered the establishment Democratic candidate and received an endorsement from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee.

candidates.name: Matthew Dunlap
candidates.summary: Matthew Dunlap is the Maine State Auditor and a former two-term Maine Secretary of State. He previously served in the Maine House of Representatives and gained national attention when he served on President Donald Trump's Presidential Advisory Commission on Election Integrity, which he later challenged in court. Dunlap is running as a progressive, supporting Medicare for All and a fair immigration system.

candidates.summary: Paige Loud is a social worker and citizen of the Cherokee Nation running on a progressive platform including universal healthcare, guaranteed food and housing, and free higher education. She supports single-payer Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and the Homes for All Act. Loud conceded the Democratic primary on June 10, 2026, after trailing in the initial vote count.

forecast.rationale: This open-seat race in Maine's 2nd District is rated tilt R with low confidence due to sparse evidence. The district has a Republican presidential lean — Donald Trump carried it in both 2020 and 2024 — and the retirement of Democratic incumbent Jared Golden removes the ticket-splitting advantage that helped Dems hold the seat. Republican nominee Paul LePage is a former two-term governor with universal name recognition across the state, giving the GOP a clear early structural edge. However, LePage is also a polarizing figure, and Democrats have a competitive primary (unresolved after June 9, heading to ranked-choice tabulation) that could produce a moderate nominee such as Joe Baldacci (DCCC-backed former Bangor mayor and state senator) who may be well-suited to this district. The lack of any general-election head-to-head polling — the only poll reference is a primary-period SurveyUSA survey without general-election matchups — combined with the unresolved Democratic nomination creates significant uncertainty. Republican advantage is narrow and contingent on both the Democratic nominee and LePage's ability to reassemble his statewide coalition in a federal race.
